title: Alternative employment can coexist with an unfair-dismissal remedy and an unresolved payment boundary
source_unit: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2023] FWC 2632, Westrip dismissal case

observations.period: May 9–June 13, 2023; dismissal, alternative employment, and compensation order

denominator.unit: publicly identified adjudicated worker case; no population denominator

assessed_no_remuneration_interval.unit: weeks of likely lost remuneration assessed by the Commission

ordered_compensation.unit: Australian dollars gross less tax, ordered within 21 days

reinstatement.value: not sought; compensation ordered in lieu of reinstatement

worker_level_payment_receipt.unit: missing payment execution and receipt evidence

observations.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision; case-level dates, alternative employment, assessed income gap, non-return, and remedy order are kept separate from payment receipt and later recovery.
observations.uncertainty: One case cannot estimate dismissal, alternative-employment, compensation, payment, or recurrence rates. The decision does not enumerate the full offer set, search effort, job duration, household effects, or later trust and exit.
observations.subgroup: One qualified mechanic dismissed after disputed conduct and performance concerns; the Commission found the dismissal unfair while recognizing a valid underlying reason and limiting the remedy scope.
observations.counterinterpretation: Alternative employment at slightly higher pay may limit assessed loss without restoring the original relationship, resolving the interim income gap, or proving durable recovery; an order is not payment receipt.

related_sources.claim: Official Fair Work Commission decision-search route used for the case recheck.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the committed project ledger because the direct FWC PDF route returned HTTP 403 during this promotion.
reproduction_audit.access_boundary: No public payment-compliance filing, worker receipt record, later employment follow-up, household outcome, or exit record tied to the case reference was located in the project recheck.

boundary: This record adds one primary adjudicated case with observed dismissal, alternative employment, a five-week transition, an assessed interim income gap, non-return through compensation in lieu of reinstatement, and an ordered remedy. It does not establish payment receipt, household recovery, durable trust, recurrence, collective action, switching, or exit.
